artifacts.summary: Three verdicts: Rabin's theorem IS tied to a held source (Thomas 1997 Thm 6.20, with the countable-branching extension and a self-contained proof); FrameClass.ZTime is exactly D=Z with all bi-infinite walks, machine-checked, with two named residues (no L-plus carrier normalization, Saturation paper-level on infinite carriers); and NO usable finite certificate is inheritable -- the finite model property is refuted outright, with Thomas's Basis Theorem naming finite presentation as the shape to aim at instead. Also records that the archived Probe476.fmp_false no longer elaborates (reports sorryAx) and the one-term repair that restores it.

user_decision.question: Decidability of the stability-modal language at integer time is NOT known -- it is a five-step paper argument whose one recalled ingredient is now held and whose other four steps are unverified. Should the downstream stability-modal design tasks be started anyway?
options: Start them, reframed as 'construct a decision procedure' rather than 'formalize a known-decidable target' -- the certificate design must supply its own finiteness argument either way
Hold them until the MSO argument's four unverified steps are discharged, or at least until the L-plus carrier normalization is landed
Abandon the line on the grounds that the target is not known decidable
user_decision.recommended: Start them, reframed as 'construct a decision procedure' rather than 'formalize a known-decidable target' -- the certificate design must supply its own finiteness argument either way
